management_principles: Discuss pros/cons of tissue expander/implant versus autologous DIEP free flap reconstruction:

Tissue Expander/Implant: shorter initial surgery (2 hrs), quicker initial recovery (2-3 weeks), but requires series of outpatient saline inflations, second exchange surgery, and carries lifelong risk of capsular contracture, implant rupture, and poor cosmetic outcome if post-mastectomy radiation is required
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 52F breast cancer patient evaluating immediate vs delayed and implant vs autologous tissue breast reconstruction options prior to mastectomy.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 74, BP 124/78, BMI 28.5. Breast exam reveals moderate ptosis bilaterally with right upper outer quadrant biopsy scar. Abdominal exam shows adequate lower abdominal pannus excess with transverse Pfannenstiel C-section scar, soft abdomen without ventral hernia. CT Angiography of deep inferior epigastric perforators confirms robust bilateral dominant perforating vessels through the rectus abdominis muscle.
reference_soap.assessment: Candidate for Immediate Post-Mastectomy Breast Reconstruction comparing Two-Stage Tissue Expander/Implant vs Autologous DIEP (Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator) Free Flap.
reference_soap.plan: Provide comprehensive decision aids. Discuss pros/cons: 1. Tissue Expander/Implant: shorter initial surgery (2 hrs), quicker initial recovery (2-3 weeks), but requires series of outpatient saline inflations, second exchange surgery, and carries lifelong risk of capsular contracture, implant rupture, and poor cosmetic outcome if post-mastectomy radiation is required. 2. Autologous DIEP Free Flap: microsurgical transfer of lower abdominal fat and skin utilizing perforator vessels without sacrificing rectus abdominis muscle (preserving core strength); longer surgery (6-8 hrs) and recovery (4-6 weeks), but provides permanent, natural-feeling autologous tissue that ages naturally and tolerates radiation superiorly, plus aesthetic abdominal donor site contouring.

learning_objectives: Compare prosthetic (tissue expander/silicone implant) vs autologous tissue (TRAM/DIEP/PAP flaps) breast reconstruction regarding surgical complexity, recovery, and longevity

Explain the anatomical evolution and functional superiority of the Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator (DIEP) free flap over the muscle-sacrificing TRAM flap in preserving rectus abdominis core strength
Evaluate the impact of Post-Mastectomy Radiation Therapy (PMRT) on reconstruction choice (radiation significantly increases implant capsular contracture and extrusion rates)
Outline microsurgical monitoring protocols for free tissue transfer patency (Doppler checks, color/turgor assessment, capillary refill)
